is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae sensu lato (An. gambiae s.s. and An. arabiensis) in Tanzania (page 2, Methods).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995S (kdr-east) (Table 4, page 7).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 4 (page 7) provides genotype counts (LL, LS, SS) and sample sizes (N) for L1014S kdr in multiple populations.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from nine field populations in Tanzania in 2011 (page 4, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field collections, bioassays, and molecular analyses.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies locations at the district/city level: Ilala, Temeke, Kinondoni, Rundugai, Kikafu, Kawaya, Zeneti, Kilulu, and Muheza (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study states mosquitoes were collected in 2011 (page 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new, specific collection of nine populations in 2011 for this research.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype data is provided in Table 4.

assessment.summary: This study investigated insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations from nine sites in Tanzania, categorized by environment (urban, agriculture, low pesticide). It performed bioassays, species identification, kdr genotyping, and microarray-based gene expression analysis. The L1014S kdr mutation was found at high frequency in An. gambiae s.s. in urban areas, while An. arabiensis showed higher resistance to deltamethrin in agricultural areas, linked to metabolic resistance mechanisms.
